name: South Deep
overview: South Deep is a world-class, bulk mechanized underground gold mine located in the Witwatersrand Basin near Westonaria, Gauteng. It possesses one of the world's largest gold mineral reserves and operates at depths between 2,400m and 3,000m below surface.
locationDetails: West Rand District, Gauteng Province, South Africa (~45 km south-west of Johannesburg)

keyMetrics.label: Attributable Production (H1 2026)
keyMetrics.source: Gold Fields H1 2026 Operational Results (25 August 2026)

sustainabilityHighlights: Khanyisa 50MW solar plant reduces carbon footprint by ~110,000 tonnes CO2e annually
9 Host Community Trusts funded for education, youth employment and health programs
Over 80% water recycled and reused in closed-circuit operations
operationalHighlights: Steady grade improvements through optimized destress mining and development rates
Advanced 'South of Wrench' exploration drilling program underway
Zero fatalities achieved in H1 2026 reporting period

name: Tarkwa
overview: Tarkwa is a premier open-pit gold mine located in south-western Ghana. It is one of the largest single gold producers in West Africa, operating multiple open pits across the Tarkwaian paleoplacer formation.
locationDetails: Tarkwa, Western Region, Ghana (~300 km west of Accra)
sustainabilityHighlights: Gold Fields Ghana Foundation investments exceeding $100M into local infrastructure and education
Certified ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 across processing and pit facilities
Comprehensive progressive land rehabilitation and reforestation
operationalHighlights: Consistent throughput delivery across Pepe and Teberebie pits
High plant availability (>94%) across the CIL circuit
Excellence in environmental safety management

name: Salares Norte
overview: Salares Norte is a newly commissioned, high-grade open-pit gold-silver mine situated in the High Andes of the Atacama region at elevations between 3,900m and 4,700m. It represents a key growth asset in Gold Fields' global portfolio.
locationDetails: Diego de Almagro, Atacama Region, Chile
sustainabilityHighlights: State-of-the-art dry stack filtered tailings ensuring maximum water conservation and seismic safety
Rigorous Short-Tailed Chinchilla protection and habitat preservation protocols
Local community engagement with indigenous Colla communities
operationalHighlights: First gold poured and ramp-up trajectory progressing toward design capacity
Advanced cold-weather operational protocols for high-altitude Andean conditions

name: Cerro Corona
overview: Cerro Corona is an established open-pit copper-gold porphyry operation located in the Hualgayoc district in northern Peru, producing high-grade copper concentrate with gold content.
locationDetails: Cajamarca Department, Northern Peru (~600 km north of Lima)
sustainabilityHighlights: Over 90% workforce recruited from Peru and surrounding Cajamarca communities
Pioneering water stewardship providing clean community water supply to Hualgayoc
operationalHighlights: Stable copper-gold metallurgical recoveries exceeding 85%
In-pit tailings transition planning advancing safely

name: St Ives
overview: St Ives is a foundational Australian gold mining complex located in the Eastern Goldfields of Western Australia, operating both underground and open pit mines across Lake Lefroy.
locationDetails: Eastern Goldfields, Western Australia (~80 km south of Kalgoorlie)
sustainabilityHighlights: Multi-megawatt renewables microgrid deployment to power Lefroy operations
Strong reconciliation partnerships with Traditional Owners (Ngadju People)
operationalHighlights: Invincible underground mine producing high-grade ore consistently
Exploration drill successes expanding life-of-mine extensions

name: Granny Smith
overview: Granny Smith is an underground gold mine located near Laverton in Western Australia, known for its deep Wallaby ore body and pioneering gas-solar-battery microgrid.
locationDetails: Laverton, Western Australia (~740 km north-east of Perth)
sustainabilityHighlights: Award-winning hybrid microgrid integrating solar PV, reciprocating gas engines, and lithium-ion batteries
Progressive rehabilitation on legacy historical waste landforms
operationalHighlights: Zone 110 and Zone 120 development at Wallaby maintaining steady grade output
Underground autonomous drilling technologies increasing safety and drill rate

name: Agnew
overview: Agnew is an underground gold mine near Leinster, Western Australia, celebrated as a global mining benchmark for renewable energy integration with a landmark wind-solar-battery microgrid.
locationDetails: Northern Goldfields, Western Australia (~23 km west of Leinster)
sustainabilityHighlights: Agnew Microgrid features 5 wind turbines (18MW), 10,000 solar panels (4MW), and a 13MW/4MWh battery
Benchmark for zero-emission underground mining studies
operationalHighlights: Waranga and New Holland underground extraction delivering high metallurgical recovery
Active sub-surface exploration identifying extensions at Barren Lands

name: Gruyere
ownership: 50% Gold Fields, 50% Gold Road Resources (Manager: Gold Fields)
overview: Gruyere is a Tier 1, low-cost, long-life open-pit gold mine located in the Dorothy Hills Greenstone Belt of Western Australia, operated by Gold Fields in a 50/50 joint venture.
locationDetails: Yamarna, Western Australia (~200 km east of Laverton)
sustainabilityHighlights: 13MW solar farm and battery installed supplying green power to remote Yamarna region
Close ongoing collaboration with the Yilka native title holders
operationalHighlights: Deep open pit mining optimization with improved excavator and haul truck productivity
Process plant optimizations achieving sustained 1,100 tph throughput

name: Windfall Project
ownership: 50% Gold Fields, 50% Osisko Mining (Gold Fields Joint Venture)
overview: The Windfall Project is an advanced, high-grade underground gold development project located in the Abitibi greenstone belt of Quebec, Canada, operated in a joint venture with Osisko Mining.
locationDetails: Urban-Barry greenstone belt, Eeyou Istchee James Bay, Quebec, Canada
sustainabilityHighlights: Collaborative Impact Benefit Agreement planning with the Cree First Nation of Waswanipi
Designed for low-carbon hydroelectric power from the Quebec grid
operationalHighlights: Extensive underground exploration decline excavated exceeding 12 km
Bulk sampling programs validating metallurgical recovery projections (>95%)

name: Damang (Transferred)
ownership: Transferred to Government of Ghana (18 April 2026)
overview: Damang was historically operated by Gold Fields in south-western Ghana. As disclosed in the official H1 2026 Review of Operations, ownership of the Damang mine was formally transferred to the Government of Ghana on 18 April 2026. It is no longer an active Gold Fields operating asset.
locationDetails: South-western Ghana (~30 km north of Tarkwa)
